newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-TATAURANGI WIPES OUT EIGHT-SHOT DEFICIT TO TAKE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TATAURANGI WIPES OUT EIGHT-SHOT DEFICIT TO TAKE TITLE.

text.p: New Zealand golfer Phillip Tataurangi came from eight shots behind overnight to win the Australian PGA championship by one stroke on Sunday.
Tataurangi fired a five-under-par final round of 67 to win the A$400,000 tournament (US$316,000) at a windswept New South Wales course with an aggregate of 279.
The New Zealander's final round was in stark contrast to that of overnight leader Chris Gray of Australia, who had led by six shots.

Gray, still looking for his first title in a six-year professional career, slumped by recording a final round 78 to finish with compatriots Anthony Painter and Wayne Smith in a three-way tie for fourth on 282.
Australians Rodger Davis and Peter Lonard tied for second on 280, Davis matching Tataurangi with a 67.
Davis appeared to be heading for the title until an error in club selection saw him drop a shot at the par three 17th hole.
Tataurangi assumed that, because of Gray's substantial lead, he would be playing for second at best after being equal sixth overnight.
The New Zealander did not realise he was in front until he looked at the leaderboard as he went to tap in a short putt for par at the final green.
He later told reporters he had taken no notice of the loud support he had received from family members at the course.
"They whistle, hoot and roar whether it's birdie, par or bogey," he said.
